title: The graph: why SRS needs a graph element

sections.name: claim
sections.label: Claim
sections.content: SRS needs a graph element (the owner, 2026-10-30, vignette in conversation 2026-10-29). In the owner's own words the need is for relationships and links; no vignette uses the word graph.

sections.name: story
sections.label: The story so far
sections.content: SRS was always a graph: records joined by typed, binary relations, and in September we ruled that meaning lives in relations. What was missing was evidence for a graph surface, so every relation feature nobody used was removed with a return trigger. Those triggers are now firing: a third-party demo had to restate 296 relations as membership to print one document, clients rebuild the same walks, people cannot see what links to what, and federation's return is ratified. The need the evidence supports is narrow: one-hop selection by relation, visible links, and a bounded walk in the core. It is not a graph query language.

sections.name: parts
sections.label: The parts
sections.content:
1. People need to see what links to what.
2. Documents need to select records by relation.
3. Agents and clients walk the graph themselves.
4. Relation integrity: what is done and what is missing.
5. The graph across repositories.
6. Against: why graph features were removed and what to avoid.
Each part is a section below this one, with its evidence inside it.

sections.name: open
sections.label: Open questions
sections.content: More than one hop? Where a graph view lives. Walk as service or query axis. Constraints first? Demand beyond the owner's projects. No affirmed problem names relation selection itself; SP-24 and SP-48 carry it today.
